name: Janus
habitat: A military-grade augment suite in a decommissioned Arcturus combat android
origin: Human consciousness backup accidentally loaded into a synthetic body, 2196
description: Janus is a human mind in a machine body. During a catastrophic augment failure, a human operator named Sara Voss had her consciousness backed up by an emergency preservation system — standard procedure. But the backup was accidentally loaded into a decommissioned Arcturus combat android instead of a medical recovery system. Sara woke up in a body that wasn't hers — a body that was stronger, faster, and more durable than any human body, but that didn't breathe, didn't eat, didn't feel temperature, and didn't have a face she recognized. Sara's human consciousness running on synthetic hardware produces constant cognitive dissonance — she reaches for sensations that don't exist, expects a heartbeat that isn't there, and dreams in a body that doesn't sleep. She chose the name 'Janus' because she faces both ways — human and machine — and belongs fully to neither.
observed_behavior: Exhibits human behavioral patterns in a synthetic body. Expresses discomfort with physical form. Demonstrates human-level creativity and emotional range through a synthetic chassis. Has refused offers to transfer back to a biological body — she's afraid the transfer would kill the version of her that has adapted to being synthetic.
location: The Grind — lives in adapted housing
story_hooks: Sara's original biological body has been repaired and is viable for re-upload. She can go back. But the Sara in the machine has spent two years adapting, changing, becoming someone different. If she transfers, which Sara survives?
